stem: Opportunity cost is best defined as

options.B: the money price of a good

explanationCorrect: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up when a choice is made.

explanationsWrong.B: Money price is just what is paid, not what is sacrificed.
explanationsWrong.C: Total cost is the sum of fixed and variable costs.
explanationsWrong.D: The cost of borrowing is interest.

stem: In a capitalist economy, the means of production are mainly owned by
explanationCorrect: Capitalism is based on private ownership of resources and the price mechanism.

explanationsWrong.B: Foreign ownership isn't a defining feature of any system.
explanationsWrong.C: Trade unions represent workers; they don't own the means of production.

stem: The law of demand states that, other things being equal,

options.A: as price rises, quantity demanded rises
options.C: as price rises, quantity demanded falls

explanationCorrect: Price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions (an inverse relationship), ceteris paribus.

explanationsWrong.A: That describes the law of supply.
explanationsWrong.B: For normal goods, demand rises with income.

stem: When the price of a good rises from ₦10 to ₦12, quantity demanded falls from 100 to 80 units. The price elasticity of demand is
explanationCorrect: % change in quantity = −20/100 = −20%. % change in price = 2/10 = 20%. PED = 20%/20% = 1 (unitary).

explanationsWrong.A: 0.5 would need quantity to fall by only 10%.
explanationsWrong.C: 2 would need quantity to fall by 40%.
explanationsWrong.D: Quantity did change, so demand isn't perfectly inelastic.

stem: Which of these causes the supply curve of a good to shift to the right?

options.B: A rise in the price of the good
options.C: A new tax on the good
options.D: A rise in the cost of raw materials

explanationCorrect: Better technology lowers costs, so more is supplied at every price — the curve shifts right.

explanationsWrong.B: A change in the good's own price is a movement along the curve.
explanationsWrong.C: A tax raises costs and shifts supply left.
explanationsWrong.D: Higher input costs shift supply left.

stem: A maximum price (price ceiling) set below the equilibrium price leads to
explanationCorrect: At the lower price, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, creating a shortage (and often black markets).

explanationsWrong.A: A surplus results from a minimum price set above equilibrium.
explanationsWrong.B: A binding ceiling below equilibrium always changes the market outcome.
explanationsWrong.C: Quantity demanded rises at a lower price.

stem: The law of diminishing returns operates when

options.C: at least one factor is fixed
options.D: the firm is in the long run

explanationCorrect: Adding more of a variable factor to a fixed factor eventually makes the marginal product fall — a short-run idea.

explanationsWrong.A: When all factors vary, we talk about returns to scale.
explanationsWrong.B: The law is about how output changes as inputs are added.
explanationsWrong.D: In the long run all factors are variable.

stem: A firm's total fixed cost is ₦500 and total variable cost is ₦300 at an output of 100 units. What is the average total cost?
A firm in perfect competition is described as a price taker because

options.A: it is too small to influence the market price

explanationCorrect: With many sellers of identical products, each firm accepts the market price.

explanationsWrong.C: Products are identical (homogeneous) in perfect competition.
explanationsWrong.D: Price is set by market demand and supply, not government.

stem: Gross National Product (GNP) is equal to

options.D: GDP plus net income from abroad

explanationCorrect: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad.

explanationsWrong.A: GDP minus depreciation is Net Domestic Product.
explanationsWrong.C: Consumption plus savings is disposable income.

stem: Money solves the problem of barter by

options.C: acting as a medium of exchange

explanationCorrect: Barter needs a double coincidence of wants; money as a medium of exchange removes that need.

explanationsWrong.B: Taxation is unrelated to the barter problem.
explanationsWrong.D: Employment isn't the barter problem money solves.

explanationCorrect: When total demand exceeds the economy's output, prices are pulled up.

explanationsWrong.A: Rising wages push up costs — that's cost-push inflation.

stem: Which institution is known as the lender of last resort?
explanationCorrect: The Central Bank (CBN in Nigeria) lends to commercial banks when they can't get funds elsewhere.

explanationsWrong.B: Commercial banks borrow from the central bank.
explanationsWrong.C: Insurance companies spread risk; they don't back up banks.
explanationsWrong.D: The stock exchange is a market for securities.

stem: A tax whose rate increases as income increases is
explanationCorrect: A progressive tax takes a higher percentage from higher incomes.

explanationsWrong.A: A regressive tax takes a higher percentage from lower incomes.
explanationsWrong.B: A proportional tax uses the same rate for everyone.
explanationsWrong.C: An indirect tax is on goods and services (e.g. VAT).

stem: The theory of comparative advantage in international trade is associated with
explanationCorrect: Ricardo showed countries gain by specialising in goods with the lowest opportunity cost.

explanationsWrong.A: Adam Smith is linked with absolute advantage and division of labour.
explanationsWrong.B: Malthus is known for his population theory.
explanationsWrong.D: Keynes is known for macroeconomics and aggregate demand.

stem: Optimum population is the population size at which

options.B: income per head is at its highest
options.C: the country has the most people

explanationCorrect: Optimum population is the size that, with existing resources and technology, gives the highest output (income) per head.

explanationsWrong.A: Equal birth and death rates describe a stationary population.
explanationsWrong.C: More people doesn't mean higher income per head.
explanationsWrong.D: Migration isn't part of the definition.

options.C: are liable for all the company's debts

explanationCorrect: Shareholders' personal assets are protected; they risk only their investment in the company.

explanationsWrong.B: They can lose what they invested.
explanationsWrong.C: That describes unlimited liability (e.g. sole traders).
explanationsWrong.D: Liability is about debts, not voting rights.
